candidate_name: Cyprus LNG export point (FLNG or onshore liquefaction) — aspiration
sponsor_or_proposer: Republic of Cyprus / Ministry of Energy, Commerce & Industry (Energy Minister Yiorgos Papanastasiou)
current_state: Verbal-intent only. At an energy symposium the Energy Minister stated the goal for Cyprus to become 'a point of LNG export' from East-Med reserves, naming two theoretical routes (an offshore FLNG unit OR an onshore liquefaction terminal). No sponsor, no designated site, no capacity, and no concrete step (no FEED/permit/MOU/site selection) for any Cyprus-sited liquefaction facility. Note: the existing committed East-Med export developments (Aphrodite Block 12, Cronos Block 6) liquefy in EGYPT (Damietta), not Cyprus — see qa note — so this aspiration would be a genuinely new, currently non-existent Cyprus-sited export terminal.
missing_threshold_elements: sponsor (specific developer, not the government); location (specific site — offshore-vs-onshore not chosen); concrete step (no FEED/permit/MOU/site selection)
watch_for: A named developer or SPV; a chosen site (offshore FLNG block vs an onshore site, e.g. Vasilikos); a FEED/pre-FEED award, MOU, or licensing/regulatory pre-filing for a Cyprus-sited liquefaction plant; any FID schedule. Re-check ~6-12 months.
notes: best_lead_url verified via url_verifier.py (tokens LNG, Κύπρος → PASS). Greek-language trade press (Energymag). WebFetch read of the article confirms 'general aspiration rather than a concrete project' with 'no designated site, capacity, or sponsor' and 'no FEED study, permits, or formal agreements.' Distinct from the existing GEM cancelled export record T100001048370 (old DEFA liquefaction at Vasilikos), which is a different, defunct proposal.
